paper_id: Genomic insights into the evolution of Echinochloa species as weed and orphan crop
title: Genomic insights into the evolution of Echinochloa species as weed and orphan crop
motivation: Barnyard grasses cause 50-70% rice yield loss yet include domesticated millets; genomic basis of this dual role is unknown
problem_framing: Complex allohexaploid/allotetraploid genomes impede understanding speciation and adaptation; species delimitation is difficult
key_insight: Contrasted NB-ARC disease-gene contraction in Echinochloa vs expansion in wheat reveals fitness-cost-driven adaptation strategy
method_signature: DipHiC diploid-assisted polyploid genome scaffolding + population-scale resequencing of 737 accessions
evaluation_criteria: Assembly quality validated by BUSCO, LAI scores, read mapping rates, and subgenome-specific k-mer partitioning
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Details of E. colona hexaploidization could not be uncovered because of the lack of parental genomes
evidence_for_taste: excellent resources or systems for understanding plant tolerance to stress
marked contraction in the sizes of gene families related to biotic stress response
substantial impact of ILS on phylogenetic inference
genetic exchange events (introgression) rather than ILS drove topological incongruence
thinking_moves: 用小麦多倍体演化框架类比Echinochloa polyploidization
将基因家族拷贝数变化与适应度成本关联解释 weeds 高适应性
用KS分布峰值+物种树一致性+QuIBL三角度交叉验证phylogeny
通过ABBA-BABA统计量化种间渐渗对遗传多样性的贡献
